text:
sam: FYI — after the kernel rollout to nodepool gpu-us-west2-rc (yesterday 02:30 UTC) we have ~6 nodes in NotReady and NoSchedule. Kubelet log shows the NVIDIA modules failing, device-plugin -> CrashLoopBackOff. Autoscaler isn't scaling down because nodes are tainted and pods stuck.

priya: Ugh. Is this the same kernel patch that landed cluster-wide? any node images pinned?

sam: It was the managed-ubuntu-6.1 -> managed-ubuntu-6.2 kernel bump. Quick log snippet from one node: 

```
Oct 18 03:11:02 gpu-node-12 kernel: nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
Oct 18 03:11:02 gpu-node-12 kernel: nvidia: Unknown symbol mm_rwlock_init
Oct 18 03:11:02 gpu-node-12 systemd: nvidia.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Oct 18 03:11:02 gpu-node-12 kubelet: E1020 03:11:02.123456 1 device_plugin.go:89] failed to register with kubelet: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
Oct 18 03:11:05 gpu-node-12 kubelet: NodeStatus: NotReady kubelet.kubernetes.io/last-known-healthy: 2026-10-18T03:11:05Z
```

priya: Those Unknown symbol errors usually mean the nvidia module built against previous kernel ABI. Did DKMS run?

sam: DKMS failed during update. The image update skipped rebuilding nvidia-dkms due to missing headers. driver package is present but module not loaded. `nvidia-smi` not found inside node.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaleDown: failed to remove instances [gpu-node-12 gpu-node-14], reason: nodes have non-evictable pods: [daemonset/gpu-monitor daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin], scale-down disabled by taint/noSchedule.

oliver: Can we cordon + drain affected nodes and force-recreate? If device-plugin is a daemonset it's non-evictable; that prevents autoscaler from reclaiming. Quick mitigation: cordon the nodes and create replacement nodes with older image or re-run driver install via a privileged DaemonSet.

jen_oncall: Cost note — these orphaned GPUs keep billing. If autoscaler can't remove them, we should prioritize either reprovisioning or rolling back kernel. Raising a formal incident? :rotating_light:

priya: I'm wary of a mass rollback. Safer path: create a one-off privileged DaemonSet that installs matching kernel headers and triggers DKMS compile (or installs the packaged nvidia-driver-525). Then kubelet should load the module and device-plugin will stabilize. I'll draft the DaemonSet spec now.

sam: I started cordoning the worst nodes and moved batch jobs off. Confirmed pods that require GPUs are Pending due to NoSchedule taint. I also disabled cluster-autoscaler scaleDown for the cluster temporarily to avoid churn.

oliver: Plan B if the driver reinstall fails: reprovision a small nodepool with image pinned to managed-ubuntu-6.1, migrate the workloads, then drain/delete broken nodes. That avoids touching kernel fleet-wide. Scheduling a maintenance window in 30m.

jen_oncall: Please post any commands you run here and tag infra oncall. I'll open an incident and ping finance if billing spike persists.

priya: DaemonSet install snippet I'm going to run (privileged init container):

```
initContainers:
  - name: install-driver
    image: ubuntu:22.04
    securityContext:
      privileged: true
    command: ["/bin/bash","-c","apt-get update && apt-get install -y linux-headers-$(uname -r) dkms && apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-525 && modprobe nvidia || true"]
```

sam: Running that on 2 nodes first as a canary. I'll post logs.

oliver: Also file a support ticket with cloud provider; their image update pipeline might have omitted headers. Good catch.

priya: Link to GPU infra runbook for driver issues: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-failures (referenced)

jen_oncall: Thanks — keep updates in this thread. I'll add the incident channel and move to incident mode if we see >10 nodes affected or billing spikes. :thumbsup:
